title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 13-14
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 13 to 14 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'रुद्रो बहुशिरा बभ्रुर्विश्वयोनिः शुचिश्रवाः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 13 to 14 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 13 to 14.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 13 to 14** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **रुद्रो बहुशिरा बभ्रुर्विश्वयोनिः शुचिश्रवाः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**रुद्रो बहुशिरा बभ्रुर्विश्वयोनिः शुचिश्रवाः । अमृतः शाश्वतः स्थाणुर्वरारोहो महातपाः ॥** **सर्वगः सर्वविद्भानुर्विष्वक्सेनो जनार्दनः । वेदो वेदविदव्यङ्गो वेदाङ्गो वेदवित् कविः ॥**

He drives away sorrow, he has many heads, and he carries us all. The source of the universe, whose fame is pure, is that God of gods. Deathless, eternal and of great penance is he. He is everywhere, knows everything and shines like the Sun. Vishvaksena, who leads on every side, and Janardana, who protects the people, is that God of gods. He is the Veda, the knower of the Veda, its limbs, and the seer.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 13 to 14 mean?
faq.a: He drives away sorrow, he has many heads, and he carries us all. The source of the universe, whose fame is pure, is that God of gods. Deathless, eternal and of great penance is he. He is everywhere, knows everything and shines like the Sun. Vishvaksena, who leads on every side, and Janardana, who protects the people, is that God of gods. He is the Veda, the knower of the Veda, its limbs, and the seer.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
